findings.title: Missing intermediate components can turn a dangling root alias into a complete match
findings.description: The resolver retains unknown components as if traversable and later pops them for dotdot. scan checks only the final graph node, so /lib -> usr/missing/.. resolves logically to /usr although POSIX lookup fails at missing. The required root therefore does not resolve to an actual directory, yet collection succeeds.
findings.impact: False INSTALLED_FILES_MATCH/complete=true for a tree missing a usable required root; violates the binding addendum root-alias guarantee. No native admission is granted, limiting severity.

reproduction.setup: Create plain /etc, /lib64, /opt/python, /opt/venv and /usr under a temporary root. Create /lib as relative symlink with target exactly "usr/missing/.."; do not create /usr/missing. Expected manifest has all six base roots, exact four exclusions and only the /lib symlink descriptor.
reproduction.expected: FAILED_OR_INCOMPLETE because required /lib does not resolve to an actual directory.

findings.recommendation: For required-root resolution against the observed graph, require every traversed intermediate component to exist as a directory after link expansion, including the component before dotdot. Preserve the distinct permission for in-scope dangling non-root links and do not infer filesystem absence from metadata-only validation graphs (empty directories are omitted). Add a real temporary-tree RED regression and verify valid alias/dotdot cases remain accepted.
